issues.display_title: Issue #560: Bug: Add & Scan floor loses its building — scanned floor jumps to the default building (PRD #536)
issues.main_description_html:
Follow-up bug on PRD #536 (multi-building).

Description

Add Floor → Add & Scan inside a secondary building drops the level's buildingId:

  • addFloorOnce appends a blank level correctly stamped with the selected building.
  • When the scan finishes, scanAddedFloor replaces that level wholesale with txtToLevel(...) output, which carries no buildingId — the scanned floor silently migrates to the implicit default building (building 1).

Observed symptoms (all the same root cause):

  • Scan result never appears in the secondary building (the level left its scope → the editor clears).
  • Switching to building 1 flashes the scan result once, then building 1's own floor takes over.
  • Back in building 2 the floor looks empty — the scanned content actually sits in building 1.

Fix: replace the level's content in place, preserving identity fields the scan pipeline doesn't know about (buildingId, mapTransform). Defense-in-depth: collab mergeAreaMetadata restores buildingId/mapTransform from the level we already hold when a stale snapshot lacks them.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Add & Scan in a secondary building keeps the floor in that building; the scan result renders immediately
  • Retry scan preserves the stamp too
  • Applying a collab snapshot cannot strip buildingId/mapTransform
  • Unit tests cover the preserved stamp
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #567: Zoom-into-building always selects the first building (PRD #536 R28/R29)
issues.main_description_html:
Found while verifying the PRD #536 gap fixes (#561–#566). Pre-existing, not caused by them.

Description

Zooming into a building can only ever select the first building.

  • addBuilding (src/store/mapStore/buildingsSlice.ts) creates { id, name } with no mapTransform, so a second building's levels project to exactly the same model pixels as the default building's — nothing separates them on the map until someone manually places one.
  • buildingIdAtLngLat (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts) returns the first group whose transformed bbox contains the point.

Verified with a throwaway test: buildings a and b with identical 100×100 geometry, 441 points swept across the shared footprint → the hit set is exactly ['a']. Building b is unreachable at every point. The same probe shows the two outdoor shells come back geometrically byte-identical.

useAutoOutdoor feeds that hit straight into selectBuilding on the editor Map tab and on /preview, /v/[key], /embed, so "zoom into Beta" selects Alpha and re-points the active level to Alpha's top floor. R28 and R29 fail for every building except buildings[0].

Fix direction

Two halves, either of which helps: give a newly added building a default placement offset so buildings do not stack on the same pixels, and/or make buildingIdAtLngLat pick the nearest/smallest containing footprint rather than the first match.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A newly added building is visually separate from the existing ones without manual placement
  • Zooming into any building selects that building, not always the first
  • Overlapping footprints resolve to the nearest building rather than array order
  • Unit test: a point over building B resolves to B
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #568: Buildings with a blank ground floor are invisible and unreachable outdoors (PRD #536 R23/R26)
issues.main_description_html:
Found while verifying the PRD #536 gap fixes (#561–#566). Pre-existing.

Description

outdoorGeoJson skips a building whose lowest level has no geometry (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts: const ground = levels[0]; if (!ground) continue; const bbox = levelBBox(ground); if (!bbox) continue;), and buildingIdAtLngLat skips it the same way.

Probe: buildings Alpha (with area geometry) and Beta (one blank level) → the outdoor collection contains only Alpha's shell and label. Beta gets no closed outer shape (R23 says "all buildings"), no label (R26), and cannot be zoomed into (R28/R29).

Add building → Add blank floor is the canonical flow, so a building can exist in the editor and the building picker while being invisible and unreachable on the map, in preview, and on live. The empty-building editor scope work and the outdoor massing were never reconciled.

A related fringe case: a building whose lowest level is empty but whose upper floors have geometry is skipped entirely, even though it has a perfectly good silhouette one floor up.

Fix direction

Fall back to the first level that HAS geometry instead of levels[0], and decide a deliberate representation for a building with no geometry at all (a placeholder footprint, or documented exclusion).

Acceptance Criteria

  • A building whose ground floor is blank but whose upper floors are not still gets a shell
  • A fully empty building has a defined, deliberate outdoor behavior (documented either way)
  • Whatever renders a shell can also be zoomed into
  • Unit test: shell derived from the lowest level that has geometry
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #569: Collab never syncs canvasData.buildings — a peer's autosave deletes building records
issues.main_description_html:
Found while verifying the PRD #536 gap fixes (#561–#566). Pre-existing, and it silently destroys data.

Description

A collab snapshot is one level's LevelData as JSON (src/lib/collab/sync.ts) — grep -rn buildings src/lib/collab/ returns zero hits. There is no channel for the buildings array or for the per-building mapTransform.

sync.ts deliberately carries buildingId across a snapshot ("Level identity is store-only too (#536)"), which shows the level stamp was considered — the building records were not.

FloorplanEditor.tsx applies a peer snapshot as store.setCanvasData({ ...data, levels: nextLevels }) where data is the local canvasData, so a peer keeps its own stale buildings. That peer's next edit flips hasUnsavedChanges, and the editor autosaves its whole canvasData two seconds later — overwriting the other editor's buildings server-side.

Result: a building record and its placement disappear, while levels stamped with it keep a buildingId pointing at a record that no longer exists. (The orphan case is now survivable — groupLevelsByBuilding falls those levels back to the default building as of #566 — but the building and its placement are still gone.)

Fix direction

Either broadcast building records as their own message type, or stop letting an autosave write the whole canvasData when only levels were synced. Whichever lands, a peer must not be able to delete another's building by editing a floor.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Adding, renaming, or deleting a building propagates to collaborators
  • A peer editing a floor cannot drop another peer's building records
  • Per-building placement survives a collab session
  • Unit test: applying a peer level snapshot preserves local building records
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #570: Outdoor state is component-local, so toolbar/transform/preview controls can't go view-only (PRD #536 R22)
issues.main_description_html:
Found while verifying the PRD #536 gap fixes (#561–#566). Four separately-reported outdoor holes share one root cause.

Description

outdoor is the return value of useAutoOutdoor, held as local state inside Editor3DMapView.tsx and separately inside PreviewOverlay.tsx. It is not in the store — unlike mapMoveMode. So nothing outside those two components can gate on it, and every remaining R22 ("outdoor mode is view-only") hole is downstream of that:

  • EditorBottomToolbar.tsx — the Move button (setMapMoveMode(true)) cannot know about outdoor, so the user can re-arm a mode that #563's enabled: mapMoveMode && !outdoor makes inert. The toolbar renders Move as pressed and Select as unpressed while neither works, and the on-map hint claims dragging works.
  • MapTransformControl.tsx — rotate / scale / nudge / reset still commit placement to canvasData while outdoor, with no visual feedback in Active Floor scope (outdoor massing is built from each building's ground level, so shifting a non-ground floor is invisible).
  • PreviewOverlay.tsx renders PreviewControls with no !outdoor guard — the reset only fires on the transition, so Search and Direction can be reopened while outdoor.
  • useDirectionMapLayers.ts — the direction drop-pin symbol layer is a plain maplibre layer with no outdoor gate, so it draws a ground-locked teardrop over the massing on /preview, /v/[key] and /embed.

Fix direction

Move outdoor into the store (next to mapMoveMode) and gate the toolbar, the transform popup, and the preview controls on it. One change closes all four.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Move mode cannot be entered while outdoor; the toolbar shows it as unavailable
  • The transform popup cannot commit placement while outdoor
  • Search and Direction are unavailable while outdoor on the public surfaces
  • No direction pin renders over the massing
  • Unit test: outdoor state gates the placement writes
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #571: Initial fitBounds ignores per-building placement — moved buildings land off-screen
issues.main_description_html:
Found while verifying the PRD #536 gap fixes (#561–#566).

Description

getBuildingLngLatBounds (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts) projects the project-wide bbox through makePixelRotator, which honors only the project transform (mapRotationDeg / mapScale / mapOffsetX/Y). It ignores per-building mapTransform — so once placement moved onto the building frame (#548 for the popup, #561 for the drag), the initial fitBounds no longer frames where the buildings actually are.

Verified numerically: two buildings sharing a raw px footprint, Beta dragged 900 px east. getBuildingLngLatBounds returns the same ~50 m box before and after the drag, while Beta's corner projects roughly 400 m outside it. Switching to the Editor tab and back remounts Editor3DMapView (EditorCanvas renders it conditionally), which resets didFitRef and re-runs the fit — the camera frames an empty box with Beta entirely off-screen. Same on /preview, /v/[key] and /embed.

The legacy no-buildings path is unaffected: an identical drag there moves the bounds correctly, because it still writes the project offset.

Fix direction

Union the per-level bboxes projected through makeLevelPixelTransform (the same chain the geometry renders with) instead of projecting one global computeBBox through makePixelRotator.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Initial fit frames every building including ones moved by per-building placement
  • Legacy projects (project-wide offset only) frame exactly as before
  • Preview, live and embed use the same corrected bounds
  • Unit test: bounds follow a building's mapTransform
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #572: Project-wide transform becomes unreachable once a building exists
issues.main_description_html:
Found while verifying the PRD #536 gap fixes (#561–#566).

Description

Once any Building record exists, every placement control takes the building branch — MapTransformControl.tsx rotate / scale / nudge / reset, and (since #561) the drag as well. Nothing writes the project-wide transform any more.

MapTransformControl's reset clears only the building's mapTransform and leaves mapRotationDeg / mapScale / mapOffsetX / mapOffsetY untouched, so a legacy project that carried a project-wide placement before its first building was added can never be reset to identity from the UI — that transform is now permanently baked in and un-editable.

Related cosmetic issue on the same popup: the readout shows the building's scale (1 by default) while the model is drawn at the project scale, so a project sitting at 200% displays "100%".

Fix direction

Either migrate the project-wide transform onto the default building record when the first building is created, or have the reset clear both frames. The readout should show the composed value.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A legacy project with a project-wide placement can still be reset to identity after buildings are added
  • The transform popup's rotation/scale readout matches what is drawn
  • No double-applied transform after whichever migration is chosen
  • Unit test: reset returns a migrated legacy project to identity
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #576: Empty building still renders a canvas instead of the no-floors placeholder
issues.main_description_html:
Reported while testing multi-building in the editor.

Description

Adding a building leaves it with no floors, so the Floor list correctly shows nothing — but the editor canvas keeps rendering a bare grid, which reads as a drawable floor that does not exist.

EditorCanvas.tsx gates the empty-project placeholder (design #304) on hasFloors(floorConfigs, canvasData), which is project-wide. With another building still holding floors it stays true, so the placeholder never appears for the empty building.

Nothing on that grid is actually drawable: FloorplanEditor already clears the model to __empty__ when no level is in scope (#536), and the engine's change handler returns early on a null active level. So every edit made there is silently dropped — the bug is that the canvas looks alive while it is not.

Fix direction

Gate the placeholder on the same building-scoped call the Floor list makes (buildFloorOptions), so the two cannot disagree. Placeholder markup stays exactly as designed in #304.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Adding a building shows the "No floors yet" placeholder from #304 on its empty canvas
  • Switching back to a building that has floors restores the canvas
  • A project with no buildings at all keeps its current empty-project behaviour
  • Unit test: a building with no levels of its own yields an empty floor list
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #586: Map Mode: rebuild the Link to Information panel to match design #480
issues.main_description_html:
Design target #480 was never implemented. PRD #473's map-mode tasks (#474, #475, #483) were built from the PRD text on 2026-07-29 09:47 UTC; the design/information-linking branch carrying the actual design landed on 2026-07-30, ~15h later, and was never integrated. The behaviour is there — the layout is not.

Description

SelectedFeaturePanel.tsx renders two different panels today:

  • 1 object selected → the legacy per-kind card (AREA · LIVING ROOM + an Information search list + Create New Information).
  • 2+ objects selected → a 288px (w-72) text-list panel: "N selected" + Clear, a small uppercase "Link to Information" label, "Not linked to information (N)", "Linked to information (N)", "Unlink All" as a bordered button.

Design #480 is one panel for any selection count (its screenshots show it at N=1 and N=4), roughly 390px wide, built from titled sections separated by hairlines.

Scope

One panel, selectedFeatureIds.length >= 1, in this order:

  1. Header — "Link to Information" + subtitle "Review selection state before changing links." + close button.
  2. Selected Objects — label left, count right.
  3. Two stat tiles — NEEDS INFORMATION and LINKED, ghost-gray, uppercase 10px label over a large count.
  4. All-linked note — green "All selected objects are linked." replaces the Choose Information section when nothing is unlinked.
  5. Choose Information — section title + count chip, helper line "Choose one information record for all N selected object.", search field, then either RECENTLY LINKED (with a "Create New Information" button on the right) or SEARCH RESULTS + "N Results". Rows: round link-glyph tile, title, one-line description, Link action. Empty state is a ghost-gray box, not bare text.
  6. Linked Information — section title + count chip + Unlink All as red text (not a bordered button). Rows: per-kind glyph (square for Area, pin for Point — same glyph vocabulary as the object list), Area — Room 14 type line over the linked record's name, optional 2-line description, then the eye / pencil / unlink actions. Rows separated by hairlines.
  7. Toast — "meja tester" linked to 1 object. with a green check, bottom-center, replacing the current inline lastLinked text.

Constraints

  • Behaviour must not regress. Everything the current panel does stays: batch link, the ≥10 confirm (PRD #473 12.1), Unlink All, per-row edit/unlink, the Show-on-Live eye for pano points (#278), and the viewer read-only treatment (§B8 — edit affordances removed, not disabled).
  • The single-selection card carries controls the multi panel does not: the safety annotation type picker and the point "Show on live map" checkbox. Unifying the panel must not drop them — they keep a home in the merged layout.
  • Type line uses the existing KIND_LABEL + displayName from object-markers.ts; sorting stays type-then-name (PRD #473 12.3).

Acceptance Criteria

  • One panel renders for both a single and a multiple selection
  • Header, Selected Objects row, and both stat tiles match #480
  • Choose Information shows Recently Linked, Search Results with a result count, and the ghost-gray empty state
  • Linked Information rows show the kind glyph, type line, record name, description, and the eye/pencil/unlink actions
  • Unlink All renders as red text and still unlinks every selected linked object
  • A successful link raises the toast instead of inline text
  • Safety type picker and point live-map visibility still reachable for a single selection
  • Viewer sees the same information with no edit controls
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #587: Preview/live: rebuild the information card and add the photo preview modal (designs #481, #482)
issues.main_description_html:
Design targets #481 and #482 were never implemented. PRD #473's visitor-facing tasks (#488, #489, #490) were built from the PRD text on 2026-07-29 09:47 UTC; the design/information-linking branch carrying the actual design landed on 2026-07-30, ~15h later, and was never integrated. The behaviour is there — the layout is not.

Paired with the map-mode panel task so the two visitor surfaces ship together: PhotoPreviewModal is opened from PreviewInfoCard, so splitting them would leave a cross-branch dependency.

Description

PreviewInfoCard.tsx already carries the substance — photo hero with pagination and counter, hours with open/closed status, contact/website/social rows, and the fixed-footer Direction button. What differs from #481 is the layout, and the photo lightbox is a borrowed component rather than the designed one.

Scope — #481, the visitor information card

  • Description gets a Show More / Show Less toggle; today it renders as one unclamped paragraph.
  • Hours, contact and link rows adopt the design's spacing and touch targets.
  • Photo hero, close button and pagination controls take the design's treatment: round translucent controls over the image, counter pill bottom-right.

Scope — #482, the photo preview modal

Replace the borrowed FloorPreviewModal (the wizard's floor-image previewer, currently passed heading="Photos") with a dedicated PhotoPreviewModal:

  • "PHOTO PREVIEW" eyebrow over the record title, top-left
  • counter pill and close button top-right

  • #209 (implemented) puts View 360 Pano directly under the title, so it stays visible above description/photos/contacts.
  • #481 puts it in the footer, beside Direction.

PreviewInfoCard.tsx cites #209 in a comment explaining the current placement, so this is a real conflict, not an oversight.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Description collapses with a Show More / Show Less toggle
  • Photo hero controls, close button and counter match #481
  • Hours, contact, social and hyperlink rows match #481 spacing and hit targets
  • Clicking a photo opens the new PhotoPreviewModal, not FloorPreviewModal
  • The modal matches #482: eyebrow, title, counter pill, round controls, blurred dark backdrop
  • Arrow keys page the modal; Escape closes the modal without closing the info card
  • Pano button placement resolved and applied per the decision above
  • Direction button still starts direction mode only when routing is available (#490)
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

issues.display_title: Issue #585: Replace the Lift/Stairs area types with a draggable Access point object
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Today "Access" is not an object — it is a grouping layer over areas. An AreaLayer whose type is lift or stairs and which carries an accessId is a member of a connected Access group (PRD #513), and the group's floor span drives multi-level routing.

That makes a lift a polygon: to create one you draw an area and retype it, to move one you drag its vertices, and every cross-floor copy has to have its geometry refitted into the target floor's frame.

Access becomes its own point object instead — placed, selected and dragged exactly like a Point or Safety annotation, while keeping the cross-floor connection behaviour it has today. lift and stairs leave the area type picker entirely.

Scope

Data model

  • AreaType drops "lift" | "stairs" → "room" | "hallway" | "open-to-below".
  • New AccessPoint extends CreatedAt { id, x, y, accessId, type: "lift" | "stairs", name?, infoId?, accessOriginLevelId? } on LevelData.accessPoints — same shape family as SafetyAnnotation, plus the group fields.
  • accessId / availableLevelIds stay readable on AreaLayer for the load migration only.

Engine (src/lib/floorplanEditor/) — the existing "point" | "safety" annotation union gains "access": floorplan/types.ts (Model.access), bridge.ts, context.ts (AnnoSel), interactions.ts (placement, drag, marquee, shortcut), hittest.ts, draw.ts, scene3d.ts, commands.ts, selection.ts, index.ts, model-sync.ts (Lift ↔ Stair, mirroring setSafetyAnnotationType).

Group logic (src/lib/editor/access.ts) — accessMembers / accessSpan / accessAdjacent / syncSpanCache / withAccessType / withAccessInfo / withoutAccess / withAccessSpan read level.accessPoints instead of layout.areas. The group semantics do not change.

Store (src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts) — setAccessType, setAccessInfo, setAccessFloorSpan, deleteAccess retarget to accessPoints.

UI — area type radiogroup in SelectionToolbars.tsx loses Lift/Stairs and gains an Access-selected toolbar; new Add Access tool button + shortcut in FloorplanEditor.tsx; AccessList.tsx and the Access count in ObjectSection.tsx read accessPoints; Access joins the annotation kinds in objectRows.ts / SimpleAnnotationList / UnifiedObjectList so it appears under the "All" filter; SelectedFeaturePanel.tsx gains the Access case.

Map / preview — useFloorPlanLabels.ts takes its icon anchors from accessPoints rather than area type (the lift/stairs glyphs in floorLabelIcons.ts are unchanged); Access joins object-markers.ts and the marker overlays (MapObjectMarkers, PreviewOverlay, Editor3DMapView, usePreviewSelectionLayers) and searchTargets.ts.

Routing (src/lib/routing/multiLevelRoute.ts) — connectors come from accessPoints; the anchor is the point's own x/y, so areaAnchor / labelPoint drop out of the connector path. No pathfinder change needed: findPath already BFS-snaps an endpoint up to SNAP_RADIUS cells to the nearest passable cell, so an Access dropped on a wall still routes.

Decisions

No 3D slab. Access renders as a marker only. The lift/stairs area extrusion and the ghost-floor palette (GHOST_LIFT_COLOR / GHOST_STAIRS_COLOR in layer-definitions.ts) go away with it.

Legacy areas become plain rooms. The one-time load migration already wired into persistence/wizardState.ts and useWizardPersistence.ts (migrateLegacyAccess) gains a second job: for every legacy lift/stairs area, create an AccessPoint at the polygon centroid carrying the same accessId, then retype the area to "room". The drawn polygon is kept — nothing the user drew is deleted.

Deletions this enables

  • fitBoundaries() in access.ts (~60 lines scaling and clamping a cloned polygon into the target floor's wall bbox) — a point only needs its x/y clamped.
  • The preservedAccess rescue block in bridge.ts, which re-appended Access areas dropped by the positional rebuild in modelToLevel. accessPoints carry their own ids and never pass through detectRooms.
  • GHOST_LIFT_COLOR / GHOST_STAIRS_COLOR and the ghost-area areaType match arms.

Note — Go API contract

src/lib/digitalTwin/schema.ts (the /v1/predict response shape) still types AreaLayer.type as AreaType and carries availableLevelIds. Narrowing AreaType on the frontend breaks the parse if the backend ever emits "lift" or "stairs". Confirm with Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO before narrowing; if the backend can emit those values, keep a wider type at the twin boundary and normalize on ingest rather than changing the contract.

accessPoints is a new array on LevelData. If the backend canonicalizes level objects on save (it does stamp createdAt), it may need to learn the field — flag before merging.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Lift and Stairs are gone from the area type picker
  • An Access tool places a marker on click; it drags like a Point/Safety marker
  • A selected Access can be switched between Lift and Stair, and the change applies to every connected copy
  • Floor span still creates/removes connected copies across floors, and multi-level directions still route through them
  • Access shows on the map and in preview as a marker with no floor slab
  • Opening an existing project with lift/stairs areas produces one Access point per legacy area at its centroid, with the polygon retyped to room and the group's floor span preserved
  • Unit tests: migration of a legacy grouped lift; span add/remove on points; a route through a point connector
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
